title: Fullstack Developer Roadmap
summary: A balanced path for learners who want to connect frontend experience, backend logic, and product-level delivery in one workflow.
audience: Best for juniors who want broader ownership and enjoy seeing how complete features work from UI to database.

sections.title: Cross-Stack Foundations
sections.description: Build enough frontend and backend understanding to think in features instead of isolated code exercises.

items.title: Understand how product flows connect frontend, backend, and data
items.description: Learn how a user action moves through UI, API, persistence, and back into the product experience.
items.whyItMatters: Fullstack growth starts when you stop thinking of frontend and backend as separate worlds.
items.expectedOutcome: You can explain a feature end to end and identify what happens in each layer.

miniProjects.title: Feature Flow Map
miniProjects.summary: Document and implement a small feature flow such as signup, profile editing, or saved jobs.

commonMistakes.title: Only understanding the layer you wrote most recently
commonMistakes.explanation: Fullstack developers become stronger by tracing a feature through the whole system.

commonMistakes.title: Thinking only in code tasks, not user outcomes
commonMistakes.explanation: Good fullstack work connects implementation to the real experience it creates.

recommendedResources.title: Beginner System Thinking Articles
recommendedResources.note: Use beginner-friendly system overviews, not interview-heavy deep dives at this stage.

items.title: Use Next.js to connect UI, routes, and server-side behavior
items.description: Learn how a single application can manage pages, shared layouts, forms, and simple server-driven features.
items.whyItMatters: A unified fullstack framework helps junior developers practice feature delivery with less setup friction.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build a structured app where UI and backend actions feel connected instead of separate projects.

miniProjects.title: Student Portal Foundation
miniProjects.summary: Build a basic portal with login screens, dashboard routes, and simple form submissions.

commonMistakes.title: Adding many features before understanding one complete flow
commonMistakes.explanation: A smaller app with one clean end-to-end flow teaches more than many unfinished screens.

commonMistakes.title: Not separating UI concerns from data concerns
commonMistakes.explanation: That makes debugging and future growth harder even in smaller projects.

sections.title: Application Building
sections.description: Start connecting interface, business logic, and persistence into more realistic projects.

items.title: Design data models that support real product flows
items.description: Practice building schemas for users, content, progress, or jobs so features have a strong data foundation.
items.whyItMatters: Fullstack apps feel cleaner when the data model supports the product instead of fighting it.
items.expectedOutcome: You can model feature data clearly and connect it to UI flows without duplicating logic everywhere.

miniProjects.title: Mini Roadmap Schema
miniProjects.summary: Design and implement a schema for learning paths, sections, items, and user progress.
deliverables: UI view backed by stored data

commonMistakes.title: Building screens first and data thinking later
commonMistakes.explanation: That often creates repeated or unclear logic when the app starts to grow.

commonMistakes.title: Trying to design a perfect enterprise schema too early
commonMistakes.explanation: A strong junior project usually needs clear relationships more than maximum complexity.

items.title: Implement user workflows such as auth, profile updates, and progress tracking
items.description: Build features that reflect how real users move through a product instead of isolated pages.
items.whyItMatters: Internship-ready fullstack projects usually show that you can model real user behavior, not only static data.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build a working user flow from login to action to persisted result.

miniProjects.title: Learner Dashboard Flow
miniProjects.summary: Build a flow where users create a profile, choose a path, and save progress on roadmap items.

commonMistakes.title: Showing auth UI without thinking through protected behavior
commonMistakes.explanation: Fullstack apps should make it clear which actions require identity and why.

commonMistakes.title: Displaying dashboard numbers that are not connected to real data
commonMistakes.explanation: It is better to show fewer real summaries than many disconnected placeholders in portfolio work.

sections.title: Job-Ready Delivery
sections.description: Strengthen the project habits that make a fullstack portfolio feel intentional and internship-ready.

items.title: Ship one complete fullstack portfolio project
items.description: Build one app that demonstrates structure, persistence, user flows, and a clear problem it solves.
items.whyItMatters: A strong end-to-end project is one of the clearest ways to show readiness for junior or internship roles.
items.expectedOutcome: You can present a complete fullstack project with technical clarity, feature purpose, and deployment readiness.

miniProjects.title: Career Tool Prototype
miniProjects.summary: Build a simple career roadmap product with onboarding, progress saving, and one advisor-style feature.

commonMistakes.title: Adding many features but finishing none of them well
commonMistakes.explanation: Internship reviewers usually respond better to one strong product flow than many shallow extras.

commonMistakes.title: Presenting the app without explaining its problem or decisions
commonMistakes.explanation: A clear story helps others understand why the project matters and what tradeoffs you made.

items.title: Improve quality, debugging, and technical explanation
items.description: Focus on the habits that make your project easier to review, maintain, and talk about in interviews.
items.whyItMatters: Being able to explain architecture and debug fullstack issues is a big part of early-career readiness.
items.expectedOutcome: You can describe how your app is organized, how data flows, and how you solved a meaningful problem.

miniProjects.title: Architecture Walkthrough Note
miniProjects.summary: Write a short technical walkthrough for a fullstack project and improve one weak part based on that review.

commonMistakes.title: Using technologies without being able to explain why
commonMistakes.explanation: It is okay to be junior, but it is important to show reasoning and curiosity about choices.

commonMistakes.title: Fixing bugs without capturing what you learned
commonMistakes.explanation: Reflection makes you stronger and gives you better stories for interviews and mentorship conversations.
